questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

The branch of science concerned with the bodily structure of humans, animals, and other living organisms
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. Anatomy.**

 
• Gastronomy is the practice or art of choosing, cooking, and eating good food.
 
• Botany is the scientific study of the physiology, structure, genetics, ecology, distribution, classification, and economic importance of plants.
 
• Astronomy is the branch of science which deals with celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.
 
• **Anatomy** is **the branch of science concerned with the bodily structure of humans, animals, and other living organisms.**

So, only option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.

There are some dates or periods of time in the history of the world that are so ________ that everyone knows and remembers them.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2) i.e. significant.**

The required word must be similar to a word that means '**important or that can be remembered**'.

 
• Representative means typical of a class, group, or body of opinion.
 
• **Significant means important; noteworthy.**
 
• Momentary means lasting for a very short time; brief.
 
• Trivial means of little value or importance.

So, only option 2 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

If children spend too much time watching television, they can create health problems for ________.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. themselves.**

The blank should contain the pronoun which is in agreement with the subject of the sentence. The subject is 'they', so the pronoun to be used is '**themselves**'.

Let us look at the usages of the other pronouns:

 
• Itself is used with 'it'.
 
• Himself is used with 'he'.
 
• Oneself is used when the subject is referred to as 'one'.

So, only option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

__Hardly he had entered__ the station, when the train whistled.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

The correction should be made in the **order of the words** in order to make it grammatically correct. The adverb 'hardly' must be followed by the verb 'had'. The noun 'I' will come afterwards.

So, the correct phrase will be **'Hardly had he entered'.**

So, only option 2 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2) i.e. had.**

As observed from the previous sentence in the passage we can see that the word '**would**' has been used which is in the **past tense**. So, the required word in blank 1 must be the **past tense form of the verb 'have'**. The only option with the past tense form is option 2 i.e. **had**.

So, option 2 is the most appropriate answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 2.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2) i.e. didn't.**

The use of words like 'was' and 'had' indicates that the **given sentence is in the past tense**. So, we must use the verb that is in the past tense form. Only options 2 and 4 are in the past tense.

Now, it is mentioned that the person had few friends and was not a good mixer. So, the **required word must be negative**. Only '**didn't**' fits the blank.

So, option 2 is the most appropriate answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3.

The passage mentions that Bepin was not a good mixer which means he did not like to engage in pointless chat. The required word must mean similar to 'pointless or inactive'.

The correct word is **idle.**

So, option 2 is the most appropriate answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 4.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'no error'

I don’t think I meet him before.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

The **present perfect tense** refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past (e.g., we have talked before) or began in the past and continued to the present time (e.g., he has grown impatient over the last hour). In the given sentence, the speaker may have never met the person in the past. Hence, we should use the present perfect tense. 

The correct phrase is **'I have met'**.

All other segments of the sentence are grammatically correct.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

She misplaced her spectacles and now finding it difficult to read.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

The given sentence uses the conjunction 'and' to join two sentences. The first part of the sentence is talking about an event that has occurred in the past. The second part of the sentence uses '**finding**' which means it is stating something that is occurring in the **present**.

The use of the auxiliary verb 'is' is missing in option 1. **The correct phrase is 'and is now finding it'.**

Hence, only option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

The climate of Dehradun is better than Meerut.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

The given sentence is making a comparison between the climates of two places. The phrase 'than Meerut' is missing a pronoun(that) and a preposition(of) which should state that the sentence talks about the climate of Meerut. **Pronouns ****function as noun phrases used by itself to refer to something mentioned elsewhere in the sentence.** **Prepositions define the relationship between the nouns.**

The correct phrase is **'than that of Meerut**'.

All other options are grammatically correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

If __I was you __I would not sign the document.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

Clearly the given sentence is talking about a time in the past. The given situation is in **subjunctive mood** which means the speaker is stating a hypothetical situation. In this type of situation, we should use '**were**' instead of 'was'.

The correct phrase should be **'If I were you'**.

All the other options are incorrect.

So, only option 2 is correct.
